newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sam Rainsy to return to Cambodia overland.
newsitem.headline: Sam Rainsy to return to Cambodia overland.

text.p: Leading Cambodian opposition politician Sam Rainsy, an ally of ousted premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, was due on Monday to return to his country overland from Thailand, Cambodian opposition and Thai Army sources said.
"I heard that he is leaving (Europe) and will try to return to Cambodia overland," a close aide of Ranariddh told Reuters.

Sam Rainsy, a respected former finance minister with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party who was expelled from the National Assembly in late 1994 after he upset powerful political figures with his campaign against corruption, was in Europe during the recent bloody overthrow of Ranariddh by co-premier Hun Sen.

The opposition leader, who heads the unrecognised Khmer Nation Party now allied with a group of parties supporting FUNCINPEC, plans to go overland from the Thai border in order to meet some opposition politicians, officials said.

A senior FUNCINPEC source said Sam Rainsy planned to meet some party officials who had fled Cambodia because they feared for their lives after the ousting of Ranariddh and the subsequent execution of at least one senior party official.
Ranariddh was out of the country when fighting broke out and has not yet returned.
Foreign sources in Phnom Penh said at least three high-ranking FUNCINPEC officials had been executed after soldiers loyal to Hun Sen took control of the capital.
Senior party officials were said to be in hiding or had fled the country.
The foreign sources said there were reports that Ranariddh's supporters were being arrested and detained in the capital and in the provinces.
Sam Rainsy gave several news conferences in Europe last week, calling for new elections and negotiations between Hun Sen and Ranariddh to create a caretaker government.

A Thai army source based in Aranyaprathet, opposite the northwestern Cambodian border town of Poipet, said he also received information that Sam Rainsy was due to arrive there before proceeding to Cambodia.

At least 58 people were killed and up to 200 wounded when Hun Sen's troops took control of Phnom Penh in two days of fighting on July 5 and 6. Hun Sen later said Ranariddh was no longer First Prime Minister, and the party would have to find a replacement.
Hun Sen and Ranariddh formed an un-easy coalition government after a 1993 United Nations-run election. The next election was due to be held in 1998.
On Sunday Hun Sen said the country must have free and fair elections.
